title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 401
paragraphs: Another thing also contributed to this expedition, which was as follows. There was among the foreign mercenaries of Amasis a man who was by race from Halicarnassos, named Phanes, who was both capable in judgment and valiant in matters of war. This Phanes, having (as one may suppose) some quarrel with Amasis, fled away from Egypt in a ship, desiring to come to speech with Cambyses. Since he was of no small repute among the mercenaries and was very closely acquainted with all the affairs of Egypt, Amasis pursued him and considered it a matter of some importance to capture him. He pursued him by sending after him the most trusted of his eunuchs with a trireme, who captured him in Lykia; but having captured him, he did not bring him back to Egypt, since Phanes got the better of him by a trick — he made his guards drunk and escaped to Persia. So when Cambyses had resolved to march against Egypt and was in difficulty about the march — how he should get safely through the waterless region — this man came to him and, besides informing him about the other affairs of Amasis, also advised him concerning the march, telling him to send to the king of the Arabians and ask him for safe passage through this region.
